name: Rocko Daymon
caption: A wrestler who returned to the roster in December 2003 after a run in SCW, per the fed's own recap column.

identity.note: MERGED with the retired NFW row rocko-daymon-gxw-2001. MERGED. The revisit trigger the presumption named — NFW reaching tier 3 — has run, and the evidence it was waiting on arrived with the crawl. NFW's own recap voice introduces him at Brawl 1 as "a veteran from ESEN covered feds such as EPW and A1E"; NFW's own text names his finisher "The Brain Rocker" and has him work a Texas Cloverleaf. EUWC's own commentary calls the Brain Rocker "his snap piledriver with the 180 twist", uses it across at least sixteen served documents and escalates it as "Brain Rocker Redux", and has him work a Tacoma Cloverleaf. A shared invented finisher name is a move a handler carries with a character, not a label another handler lifts off a marquee, and the matching secondary submission is the same signal again. Primetime Central's own PTCpedia — neither fed's document — names Rocko Daymon in the hub-wide TEAM '06 field beside Dan Ryan, Beau Michaels and Cameron Cruise, and again in A1E in 2010, corroborating NFW's own circuit line from outside NFW. The earlier presumption's stated basis, a clean handover in time, is false on its own facts: EUWC has him wrestling in January and May 2008, after the July-September 2007 NFW run, and NFW's own recap independently remarks on the schedule he was keeping. The one honest counter-signal is recorded rather than smoothed: NFW's career sentence names EPW and A1E and does not name EUWC, and no held document names both rows. Ruled at the coordinator desk under the merge-delegation doctrine, which puts receipted evidence past the bar with the coordinator and sends genuine ambiguity to the Janitor instead.
The ACW record is one match on 26 October 2003; the IWF retrospective of his career names no ACW run, and the GXW record is already kept apart from it.

tenures.source: "Understanding the beast" (naming his sister-in-law Rebecca) and the fed's own recap column for 17–20 December 2003, marking his return to the roster after a run in SCW

"Black Dawn (2004)" (18 March 2004) and "Black Dawn 2008" (21 April 2008) Also corroborated by: The fed's own weekly sign-in threads show him returning to in-ring action by June 2009 and continuing at least through a challenge issued 9 September 2009, well past the previously recorded last appearance.
